Roxelana

Haseki Hürrem Sultan Complex (Avratpazarı)

Roxelana's first great foundation: the mosque, madrasa, soup kitchen and hospital that the former captive from Ruthenia built here as the sultan's wife.

Theme
Roxelana
District
Fatih
Period
1538–1551
Visiting
Open to visitors

The story

Before Roxelana left her mark by Hagia Sophia and at Süleymaniye, her first great foundation rose here in the Avratpazarı quarter, and it was also Sinan's first work as the sultan's chief architect.

The mosque was completed in 1538–39 and the madrasa a year later. A primary school followed, and around 1550 a soup kitchen (imaret) and a hospital (darüşşifa); the foundation deed was drawn up in 1551. Here the former captive from Ruthenia, now the sultan's wife, began a career as a patron that later reached across the empire, as far as Jerusalem.

How to visit

The complex is in the Haseki quarter, a 15-minute walk or so from Aksaray. The mosque is open to visitors outside prayer times; dress modestly, and women cover their hair. Inside you can clearly see the two domes and where the second half of the hall was added in 1612. The other buildings belong to the Diyanet training centre, so their interiors are usually not open: see them from the street, especially the octagonal stone hospital. Check access on the day.
